One of the Rubirel Guard braced something against the side of the tunnel; it looked like a glowing tripwire, only a thick, broad beam of red. He tapped the side of the odd device emitting the magic.
“Ruby Linewall in place. It’ll slow them down until the gem bursts. Halberds ready. We’re close-quarters. Reduce grips to 20%.”
The Rubirel Guard were too bunched up to swing the long halberds effectively. So one twisted something and collapsed the shaft of the metal weapon. Then they were holding axe-like weapons.
This was taking forever. Georgie’s clawed hand was sweating on his pickaxe. The Rubirel Guard said nothing until one of them spoke with a female voice.
“[Dangersense] is going off.”
“Took you long enough, Maisy. What, is your Skill on holiday or something?”
One of the others joked, and the leader snapped.
“Discipline in the squad. We have a civilian to protect.”
They stopped laughing, and Georgie saw the one called ‘Maisy’ glance at him again. Then she spoke.
“…It’s [Personal Dangersense]. Only goes off when I’m in harm’s way.”
Now, every helmeted head swung towards her. But some dipped. Georgie spoke through his spit-dry mouth.
“You ever think about keeping that kind of shit to yourself, soldier?”
She grunted.
“I thought you’d be mining out of here with that fancy pickaxe. Could have cut us a separate tunnel up.”
That was true, and Georgie might have done it. He glanced over his shoulder and saw Merls staring at him, still not even able to make a run for it himself. Drakes with crossbows, kneeling, glancing over their shoulders and falling back, rank by rank…he spoke too calmly.
“You stupid, soldier? You cut your own route out and the monsters just take that. Advance Miners never open up multiple breach points if there’s enemies in the shafts.”
Silence. Then another Rubirel Guard.
“Tactical. You’re not so bad for a damn Turnscale, Advance Miner.”
“Eat shit and die. I’m an Advance Miner, not anything else.”
How they chuckled at that. For just one moment, Georgie relaxed and felt as natural and at home with this lot as he ever had with a group. Like nothing else about him mattered, even though they knew.
He liked the company of dead men and women. It made things equal. And he just wished that wasn’t what it took to feel at home.
Then—he heard the tenor of the alarms change, and they stopped reverberating through his bones. To be more precise, they kept echoing in the ground—but now he heard them, not just the rumble.
Something was in the tunnels. Georgie stood there, pickaxe raised to throw, and he sensed it. A vibration through the ground.
He had [Lowlight Vision]. Thus, the Advance Miner was the first Drake in aeons to see the death of Naamreles coming out of the ruined City of Purity. His eyes widened as the [Light] spells illuminating the dark tunnel wavered.
Then the magic went out. Wobbling as the spell matrices destabilized. He recognized that. It wasn’t someone dispelling the magic. It was…Georgie saw a roiling mass as the light vanished. Glittering, and he inhaled the foulest scent in the world as the air shifted in their presence.
“Ancestors—[Gouging Throw]!”
He threw the pickaxe, and the first shape exploded and collapsed. Georgie pulled his claw back, and the pickaxe spun towards him. Shedding—
“Poison! Watch it!”
Maisy shoved at him, and the pickaxe clattered downwards. It had been spraying droplets of—Georgie almost reached for the relic-class item, but the Rubirel Guard grabbed it.
“Back up! Back up—seal helmet! Liquid? Gaseous—”
Then the glowing helmets emitted red light, and Georgie, weaponless, backing up, saw them. The first being of moving…sludge reared upwards until it filled the huge mining tunnel. And two eyes made of hollowed magicore turned to face the Rubirel Guard. It reached out, an arm of something so black and foul it seemed like filth incarnate.
The waste-being’s arm met six of the Rubirel Guard’s halberds, who slashed at the liquid and left spatterings across their armor. It didn’t recoil. It didn’t stop—the arm kept elongating as the roiling mass of sludge walked at them.
“Biohazard alarms going off! Poison! Contact poison! Even harmful aura—Advance Miner, get back!”
One of the Rubirel Guard’s helms blared as they kept hacking. The filth of the being splashed down and then tried to slither back towards the thing walking at them. The Rubirel Guard fell back a step; the being kept trying to reach into the cavern. So they were still hacking, but slower—slower.
Georgie saw something black and thicker than the liquid embedded in the arm they were trying to cut through. The halberds swung into the thick, ropey semi-liquid mass, and the fire magic embedded in the halberds didn’t activate. Instead, the weapons turned lifeless.
Manaless. One of the Rubirel Guard backed up, cursing.
“Armor power just dropped to 65%. Get back! What’s—”
“Magicore! That’s some kind of magicore! Give me my pickaxe!”
Georgie recognized it—the way the light spells had destabilized was exactly like how magicore absorbed concentrated earth and light magic and made [Mages] helpless. These things were—
What?
Filth Elemental? Sludge Golems? Something close. They were so foul that Georgie’s bile was rising in his throat, and they’d absorbed magicore. He expected to see flies buzzing around them, or slugs, but they were so rancid nothing could survive on them, even insects.
The Rubirel Guard fell back as their armor began to lose its magic. But they kept hacking. Maisy tore the pickaxe from her belt, handed it to Georgie. Heedless of the filth on it, he prayed his gloves were enough and threw it again.
Straight into the center of the sludge-thing’s mass. It was at the breach opening now, trying to get in. It didn’t react as one of the Rubirel Guard shouted.
“[Devastating Cleave]!”
He cut half of its body apart, revealing more filth magicore, and another of the Rubirel Guard pointed.
“[Squad: Razor Blades]. Now!”
They leapt forwards, hacking at the body emerging into the tunnel. Then—at last—Georgie saw the thing half-collapse. It became ooze, and the body stopped moving. It flowed around the Rubirel Guard’s boots, and Georgie backed up a dozen steps. Glanced over his shoulders.
Merls was ducking into the tunnel, eyes wide. Georgie hollered.
“Back up! Back up—we’re almost out—”
The Rubirel Guard were hesitating.
“The breach. We can hold it. Go—”
Then the second being of filth pushed into the tunnel, and when one of the halberds struck it in the face, the ruby blade bounced off the crystalline structure of the humanoid monster. It was seven feet tall, and it did not so much as glitter, for the ‘crystals’ were made up of the same filth.
But it was—hard.
Maisy recoiled, and a fist punched her into one of the walls. Another of the Rubirel Guard shoulder-charged the crystalline filth-monster and bounced off. All his weight and a [Ramming Charge]—he glanced up.
The punch sent him reeling past Georgie, backpedalling until he sat down. The Advance Miner didn’t know how hard you had to hit the Rubirel Guard to dent their armor, but the chestplate was bowed in. He heard a rasp.
“Hard target. It just bent my armor—”
“Fall back! Fall back now! The Ruby Linewall—”
The glowing band of ruby splintered as the second filth-monster pushed at it; it lasted for all of two seconds before the device exploded. Georgie was jogging back now, trying to drag a dizzy Maisy with him. She was way too damn heavy and stumbling—
Then he saw the horror get worse. The second filth-thing was passing by the two halves of the being the Rubirel Guard had killed when both puddles bulged. An ‘eye’ of magicore formed in each puddle. They began to ooze forwards, now no longer humanoid, but moving like a slime.
“You’ve got to be…”
The third filth-being breached the tunnel, and it was neither crystal nor horrible putty. This one was just…a floating orb.
Completely black. Dirt and other particulates were floating up towards it, and as it appeared, Georgie felt a pull on his tail. He heard Maisy whisper.
“Gravity magic. It’s off the scales for weight readings. Over ten thousand pounds—”
He just ran faster. The doom of Naamreles kept coming. These were just three. Then he heard reports shouted into his earholes. Each of the three tunnels was being breached.
There were…thousands.
And there was something else behind them. The alarms.
Something else was coming.
 
——
 
Major Shellc had in his claws a Tier 5 scroll. [Localized Earthquake]. He was debating collapsing the entire dig site, but there were people down there.
Moreover…he didn’t know if it would work. He saw [Archers] firing from above, heard the crackle of Erchirite Spears charging up. But what he saw was a hell like that of Rhir.
“The arrows aren’t working. The targets are too hard, or they just sink in—”
“[Piercing Shots] and magical munitions only. Hold the magic until we know if they absorb it. Advance Miner Georgie, are you out?”
“—Too fast—”
He was right. Not all the creatures coming up were slow. Some resembled Swamp Golems; huge, towering masses of sludge with magicore ‘bones’ that made hacking through them too difficult.
“Basic appraisal—the magicore has replaced the need for a magical crystal. We can’t snipe their cores. They’re not just golem-types. I don’t know what that is—I want it dead. Erchirite Spears! Call down the lightning.”
Something—it looked like a puddle with lots of legs. It moved fast up through one of the tunnels, chasing the [Miners]. It was climbing up the walls of dirt when the lightning hit it.
“Hard target to nail. Had to waste a [Pinpoint Target] on it.”
The Captain of the Erchirite Spears sounded a bit—nervous. Shellc’s voice was cold.
“It’s still alive.”
He didn’t have to see through the smoke or collapsing stone. Indeed, the [Major] averted his eyes and counted.
Another flash of lightning coming down. Then a third. A pause.
“Target’s dead. Oozing downwards—the area’s contaminated, sir. Likely.”
Three volleys of an Erchirite Spear company for one monster. Shellc whispered.
“Captain, how many times can your company volley in an engagement if you expend your spears’ and armor’s charges fully? Even if you have to sacrifice your gear.”
“…If we have to sacrifice our gear, thirty-five more times, sir.”
“I see. Hold until I have another target for you. Advance Miner, you’re being overrun.”
“If these idiots ran fast we’d be gone! Oh shit—”
That was when Shellc saw Georgie and six armored figures sprinting out of the lowest shafts. They saw more monsters moving up ahead of them. Shellc pointed.
“Now. Dump those chests of holding. Foreman Rolx, controlled avalanches. Knock the monsters down anywhere but our escape route.”
Dirt showered down, knocking down the monsters climbing the sides of the tunnels. Foreman Rolx struck the ground, and part of the dig site caved in—burying the climbing elementals. Shellc just watched the seven figures running upwards, dodging the monsters crawling around them.
They weren’t going to make it. A floating orb emerged out of the tunnel that Georgie’s group had fled from just as the crystal-elemental which had followed them out flexed its legs. Then—it jumped.
“Hells. They shouldn’t be allowed to do that.”
That was all Shellc said. He saw, for a moment, the elemental come up to eye-level. The [Major] drew his sword. Stabbed.
[Flashdraw]. [Distance Piercer]. [Explosive Tip].
His sword hit the flying crystal being and glanced off. Shellc grimaced as the tip of his sword exploded—and sent the being crashing down. But it didn’t do any satisfying damage. It got up and leapt again. At Georgie’s squad.
Shellc stared down into the dig site and spoke.
“Captain Asrira, fall back.”
That was what a good commander said, even if—he saw the Drake diving, still in her bandages, and twelve figures leaping down the slopes. Osthia breathed acid over the crystal elemental, who began to steam. The Sisters of Chell were throwing daggers, cursing as they wore their new leather armor.
Thirteen against—Shellc counted.
“Enemy appraisal is at four thousand and rising. Casting [Localized Earthquake]. Begin evacuating everyone.”
The ground rumbled, and his footing faltered. He saw the dig site collapsing inwards, and hoped it would slow the filth monsters. And it did…for a few seconds. Then his sense of the enemy noted them moving upwards again.
Can they dig? Shellc gritted his teeth.
They can adapt. Not good. We need to completely collapse things or take out whatever magic’s spawning them. But now he was ordering the full retreat. All his senses were screaming at him—
This was just the advance guard.
 
——
 
Georgie was running when the crystal elemental crashed down next to him and got up. It was fast. He saw the Rubirel Guard turning, but the insanely strong, tough thing was coming at them, and their only hope was to run. It was leaping, and he raised his pickaxe—
A Drake swooped down and breathed acid. She had one arm in a sling and a splinted leg, but she was still flying. Somehow, on broken wings. She drew a sword with her good hand, and the Sisters of Chell threw daggers.
—The crystal thing walked forwards, and its body bulged, then it shed its skin. Like a snake sloughing off the acid and leaving it behind. A size smaller, it came forwards, swinging a fist at Osthia, who flew back.
“Oh no.”
Boyd whispered as she threw a dagger at its face and the blade bounced off. She saw Osthia half-turn in the air, drawing breath to breathe again.
“I said don’t follow me! Fall back! Just keep the Rubirel Guard safe and retreat!”
Keep the Rubirel Guard safe—the armored Drakes hesitated, but everyone was shouting at them to run, run. The Crystal Elemental leapt again and smashed one of the Rubirel Guard into the scaffolding they were running up. The Drake in armor hacked at it, but his halberd just bounced off.
There were only two—no, three people who could damage it. Georgie lifted his pickaxe and hacked off several chunks of the crystal elemental’s body with the enchanted tip before it turned on him, and he backed up, swearing. Osthia breathed more acid, and Boyd—lifted her dagger.
[Heroic Stab].
She was shaking, and Osthia was shouting at her to run, but she reckoned she’d just seen something gleaming in the thing’s chest, revealed by Georgie’s pickaxe.
A gem, albeit foul-looking, like rainbows on sludge, in the center of its chest. Maybe…
The three of them were fighting. Darting around the crystal elemental. And then Osthia’s wings gave out. She faltered, fell, and the crystal thing raised a fist as Boyd leapt forwards. Stabbed—
Her blade went through the thing’s back and sprayed out crystals onto Georgie’s arms as he tried to grab Osthia. The [Advance Miner] recoiled, but the crystal being stumbled—head turned—and it fell forwards. Boyd stared down, and her dagger had shattered into a million pieces. But it was dead. She shot Osthia a trembling grin.
“How’dya like that? Told you I was in it. You—”
Her captain was just staring behind Boyd. Osthia’s face was calm as she rose. Boyd didn’t turn her head. She just leapt forwards—and something gouged the ground behind her. Then exploded.
When she turned her head, pieces of dirt showered down around her. She saw something—like a giant eel made of the same sludge, a thousand eyes of magical gems—twisting upwards. It had spines it fired upwards at Shellc’s forces. They exploded. Below the largest monster yet, the smaller sludge-elementals, were marching. Ahead of Georgie, Osthia, and Boyd, pursuing the Rubirel Guards who turned to look down, the shouting Sisters.
Ah.
Boyd squeezed her eyes shut. Then she glanced up.
“You can fly, right, Captain?”
Can you manage two people? One look at Osthia’s bandaged wings was the answer. The walls were sheer dirt—maybe they’d be able to climb? Boyd grinned desperately as Georgie eyed his pickaxe.
“Get out of here. I’ll collapse the tunnel on us. We’ll have time if they don’t dig us out.”
He shoved Osthia, and she spread her wings. She hesitated, regarding Boyd. Then she leapt up—and slammed into a wall. Something had plucked her out of the air and pinned her against the wall. Boyd gasped.
“Wh—”
The floating orb. It was sucking everything in. Magic, arrows—and Osthia was grabbing for purchase, trying to fly—Boyd saw it floating up, and Georgie raised his axe. Hesitated. Boyd drew a dagger.
[Heroic Stab] was on cooldown. But she had other stab-Skills. Could she lunge and—?
“Boyd, don’t—”
The Sister of Chell was smiling as she tensed. And Georgie—he shoved her back.
“Move aside, lady. This is a man’s job.”
He raised his pickaxe, bracing. Out of [Gouging Throws]. His scales were trying to pull themselves out of his face—his teeth were clenched around his cigar, and he stared at the pulsing orb. Did it hesitate? It seemed to. Then he heard those damn alarms pulse louder and swore he saw his life flash before his eyes.
It was brighter than he expected. Georgie raised the pickaxe with a shout, and then the light grew brighter. The orb floated towards him, stopped, floated back—
A spear made of brilliant, orange-pink light struck it in its center. Georgie recoiled and stopped sliding forwards. The gravity effect on him lessened. He saw the orb recoil, bulge, then absorb the spear made of light.
With…effort. It had to slowly yank the spear into it. It began floating downwards, and a second spear hit it dead-center. Then a third. The orb began to tremble. It expanded around the glowing weapons, which looked real to Georgie. A haft made of glowing light. But so detailed…
He was hesitating when something slashed through the Orb of Gravity’s center. It trembled, split in half, and then turned into a vortex which yanked Osthia, Boyd, and Georgie towards it. Imploding! It w—
The vortex vanished. The same glowing sword that had cut the orb apart swung again, and the gravity well disappeared. Then, Georgie, stumbling, came face to face with the being that had destroyed the monster. He looked down and saw his ancestors.
 
——
 
It had been a long time. So long. But some things were never forgotten, even by the turning of the wheel of ages.
A face. The face was that of a Drake. He resembled his descendants in so many ways. Perhaps…he had longer neck spines, that was all. Neck spines which were long and drooping in ways modern Drakes found unkempt, but he had threaded them with rings and beads, and they seemed like hair.
His armor was also the same. A breastplate with spread wings across the chest. And the symbol of his home, a Drake, with a claw raised upwards. The City of Purity’s emblem.
Even his boots were a perfect memory. Far thinner than a Human’s; they were made for a Drake’s clawed feet and had toe-caps made of steel. Or it would have been steel, but his body, his very nature, looked like light.
Orange and pink. Perfect to detail in every way, but no flesh. He was a magical being. No familiar. No summoned creature. Just a standard, albeit perfected—light construct.
He smiled as he swung his blade through the monster and advanced higher. Past the staring Drake holding a pickaxe identified as the property of Naamreles. Past the wounded Drake Oldblood and the Human.
Identification was required. But there was an order to his priorities. So the Drake opened his mouth and spat another spear.
That hadn’t been a power he’d had in life. But the copying spell was perfect to every other part of his nature. Even his voice.
“ALARM. TOLVEILOUKA THE WRETCHED HAS BEEN DETECTED. TO ARMS. The City of Purity marches! Monsters detected! Filth in proximity to Naamreles! Citizens, stand clear! I am—”
The eel-thing below fired more spines upwards, and two hit him. The talking Drake exploded in a shower of light magic. But his voice continued. Then, below, a hundred Drakes were advancing, pursuing the beings of rot, hacking them down, even the giant serpent. All saying the same thing.
“—Vnariss Stulvecrell, Light-Soldier! My regiment marches in defense of all that is pure and true!”
A copy of the same Drake kept advancing up the slopes, pursuing more monsters. Then another and another. There were hundreds, all with the same face. One of the versions of Vnariss turned, his boots coming together, and saluted.
“Drake citizens, {CITY UNKNOWN}, please follow me for your safety! You, sir, are you a citizen of Naamreles?”
He pointed at Georgie, and the Drake stuttered.
“Wh—h—”
Vnariss’ memory tilted his head, and he seemed to flicker for a second, in a way the Horns of Hammerad would have recognized. The same magic of the Trials of Shields…but Naamreles had given its magic to its friends.
“I did not understand that, sir. You are in distress. Please, follow me. To non-citizens of Naamreles, aspire to apply to the greatest Walled City of Issrysil. If you are worthy, even the unsuitable may polish their souls until they are reflected for eternity. Like me!”
He jabbed a thumb into his chest and smiled with all his teeth. And they saw him. Even ages later.
Vnariss Stulvecrell marched higher, and the light of the City of Purity followed him. The Putrid One’s minions had been detected. Rot had been found. He was just the first wave of the security systems.
The Purifiers were coming.
 
——
 
Osthia Blackwing didn’t know what was going on, but she could make a few inferences once the shock wore off.
We’ve found the City of Purity. Only, it’s not dead. These—someone activated the security systems. That half-Elf? Did they sense him or…?
They were fighting the monsters made of sludge. That Drake calling himself ‘Vnariss’ was engaged in combat across the dig site. He cut, hacked, spat those spears—he wasn’t nearly as good as he might have been with Skills, but there were so many of him, and his weapons cleaved through the monsters.
Most of them.
A crystal elemental like the one that had nearly killed the Rubirel Guard was fighting twenty of the glowing Drakes, smashing a fist across their ranks, but every time it shattered one, another stepped in. And their weapons barely damaged its crystal body, but they had no end—
Legions of light-Drakes. Constructs. This—
Was this the treasure? If they had this, they could field—Osthia’s mind was only focused on that smiling Drake trying to escort them to ‘safety’.
There was something about the Drake who had once been Vnariss Stulvecrell which drove the living to silence. He was old.
Oh, the constructs didn’t know it. They were just beings of light, temporarily summoned, and faithful copies. But even the template they were using was…frayed.
Like an old picture. He smiled, he fought, he spoke with those ringing tones, an icon chosen to represent the City of Purity, but he felt ancient.
Still, he marched upwards, and Osthia saw one of the Rubirel Guard above her stop, yank off his helmet, and wipe at his eyes.
Even now, he serves. Our buried cities—a myth was marching upwards. Osthia wanted to believe it was just salvation. But because she was a Drake who knew her kind—she put a hand on her sword’s hilt.
“Boyd, Georgie. Get behind me.”
She rasped, and the Drake soldier tilted its head.
“Non-citizen, you appear to be wounded. {SEARCHING DATABASE. CRIMINAL ENTRY NOT FOUND.}”
A pale, white light came from its eyes and swept Osthia up and down. She felt a tingle, but the Drake smiled.
“You are entitled to Naamreles’ mercy, citizen. Please, follow me until a supervisor can attend to you. This area is now under military law. Do not deviate from instructions.”
“Ah, c’mon, it’s like the Watch? Don’t that shit in our boots.”
Boyd was, perhaps, the fastest to pick up on the catch. The glowing Drake heard her. And its smile lessened slightly.
“Human. {SEARCHING DATABASE. CRIMINAL ENTRY NOT FOUND}. You are entitled to Naamreles’ mercy as well.”
The light flashed over Boyd as the copy of Vnariss’ eyes shone again, and then it paused. Amended its statement.
“<Criminal> class detected. Human, you are under arrest. Do not resist.”
So saying, the Drake aimed a sword at Boyd. It advanced at a fast walk, and Osthia drew her sword. Barred its way.
“Don’t. She’s with me—”
“Non-citizen, you are interfering with a military operation. Your case has been sent to a supervisor. Appraising…”
The Drake’s head turned again, and this time, the scanning of its eyes was slower. It swept Osthia up and down, and she felt naked, but kept her sword raised. What the light construct said next was where the glorious myth faded.
“Analysis complete. Drake Oldblood, 81.4% genetic viability. Congratulations, non-citizen! You are qualified for {Class 2 Citizenship}! You will be protected. Scanning…”
It hit Georgie and Boyd with the same light as they tried to back behind each other. The construct spoke.
“Analysis complete. Human, 43% viability. Ineligible for citizenship. Analysis complete. Drake, 65.5% viability. Congratulations, non-citizen! You are qualified for {Class 4 Limited Citizenship} upon approval. If you are a hired laborer, please present your card now.”
“What the heck is it talking about? This—what is this thing, Captain?”
Georgie was wide-eyed, backing up from the light construct, but it was barring the way out. Osthia just shifted.
“I think it’s from the City of Purity. It’s some kind of security system, like the Terlands’ damn Golems. But it doesn’t know the city is gone…try to get around it.”
The Drake’s face watched them as they edged around. But when Boyd tried to get to the entrance, its sword raised.
“Halt, criminal. Non-citizens, force will now be employed if you interfere.”
“Great—”
Now the legions of light-soldiers became a new threat in Osthia’s eyes. Just once, could they not find something good buried in the earth?
No one buried things that were actually good and valuable. Osthia blocked the light soldier’s path. It inspected her.
“Class 2 potential non-citizen is acting in hostile manner. Subdue. Class 3+ non-citizens are acting in hostile manner. Terminate.”
“Aw, c’mon—”
It swung its sword at Boyd’s head, and she ducked. Osthia slashed, and her enchanted sword cut across the light-soldier’s face and met resistance. Like that of hitting something hard, yet fragile. She saw motes of light spray upwards. The Drake recoiled—then spoke.
“Non-citizen. You will be placed under arrest following—”
Georgie buried his pickaxe in the Drake’s arm. The enchanted pickaxe tore the arm off the construct’s body with ease. Instantly, the construct began swinging with its remaining arm. Osthia lunged again, stabbed through its chestplate, and sprayed it with acid.
“Citiz—”
She twisted the blade and had to stab two more times. The light-soldier was heavier and harder to shift than she would have thought! But once she got it off the ground, she rammed it into a wall, and Boyd’s dagger punched into a shoulder. At last—it exploded in a shower of motes.
“Damn, it’s easier than the filth-things. C’mon, Captain, let’s run for—”
They were moving out of the tunnel when five more light-soldiers all wearing Vnariss’ face marched forwards.
“Non-citizens, drop your—”
All of them ran. Well, Osthia flew for it. She winged upwards and saw Boyd and Georgie sprinting behind her. The light-soldiers didn’t run. They marched forwards, and Osthia thought that was a good thing, easy to outrun. Then she saw their mouths opening, and one began to fire a glowing spear—
Osthia swooped them and sprayed the lot with acid. It…didn’t seem to do anything to the light-soldiers, but they regarded her, and she flew higher. Boyd and Georgie, uninhibited by others, were sprinting for it with the speed only a Sister of Chell and Advance Miner could muster. But above them…Osthia gained altitude, her wounded wings screaming, and murmured.
“Oh no.”
The wave of sludge monsters was almost gone. She had assumed that they had been the infestation that had ended Naamreles, but in fact, they were practically all vaporized already. Literally. Even the giant eel-thing was lying in pieces.
The Drake constructs were too numerous, too efficient. But that begged the question of why those filth-monsters had even been allowed to…?
The problem was now the legions of identical Drakes climbing higher. They might not have been thinking beings, but whomever had made them wasn’t stupid.
“Foreign non-citizens. You are all under arrest. Lay down your weapons. No army has been authorized within the City of Purity’s aegis. Surrender or be destroyed.”
Someone up top, Shellc perhaps, had realized the same thing as Osthia. The light-soldiers were attacking Salazsar’s [Soldiers]! Arrows were bouncing off their hard light-bodies, and they were firing arrows up, spitting spears, slashing—the Rubirel Guard were holding one of the exits to the dig site, and their armor was resisting the blades of the copies of Vnariss. For now.
“Major Shellc! That Drake claimed to be regiment-strength. It scans you, and if you’re not genetically viable or something, it’s happy to kill you!”
“Acknowledged, Captain. Get your people out of there. Hurry! Something else is coming up. Every [Mage] can feel it.”
Major Shellc’s voice was terse, and Osthia whirled. She saw Boyd sprinting up to join the small squad. Asrira’s Bitches (working name) were clustered together. Osthia almost dive-bombed them as her wings gave out.
“Captain, what the heck are those? We’re not getting paid for—”
Marrygold was aiming a hand crossbow down into the excavation site. Georgie and Boyd sprinted past the Rubirel Guard, who hauled them up as Osthia gasped.
“Just get ready. Something’s coming. We need to evacuate.”
“Evacuate? They did the job of killing those damn monsters for us. Can’t we identify ourselves or something? They’re not that hostile—”
That was Advisor Merls. Osthia and Boyd glanced at each other, and the [Wing Captain] shook her head.
“They’re unthinking automatons from another age, and they believe the Putrid One’s around! Fall back! Where’s Shellc?”
She was glad to see he was pulling the [Miners] back, but it was still slow. They were jogging across the ground—but he didn’t have enough [Soldiers].
Georgie was looking around for his team. He saw Maiss and the miners of his squad jogging towards the camp.
“Those idiots—just run! Maiss, Maiss, not that way—”
Osthia concurred. They had to launch a full evacuation. She was arguing that to Merls, who wanted to try to parlay with the light-soldiers, when her scales prickled. The shouting from below turned to screams.
Then it was light. And the final, or as Tolveilouka would have said, real guardians of the City of Light showed themselves.
 
——
 
It was not like the copy of Vnariss. He walked and spoke with the pre-programmed lines they’d used after taking his personality and form. This was something else, albeit still seeming made of light.
A brighter light. Its form was indistinct, if you could even look at it without being blinded. But when Captain Osthia shielded her eyes, she saw the vague outline.
It looked like a being with a long tail, neck spines, and claws. A Drake.
With wings.
The Purifier flew upwards in a flash of light, and when it hovered in the air, she saw a twin-halo hovering above its head. Its wings cast a nimbus of light around it that seemed to purify the very air, removing the permanent scent of cattle-dung. It had no eyes she could see, nor features.
The Purifier rotated slowly. Spotted the remains of one of the sludge monsters that the Rubirel Guard had destroyed. It flew downwards, ignoring Merls shouting at it, the Rubirel Guard backing up, weapons raised.
The Purifier was…big. It was sixteen feet tall. It moved faster than Osthia through the air, and when it pointed down, she knew it had magic. Because it ‘spoke’ with a voice as dispassionate and monotonous as what you thought a Golem’s voice would be.
It said:
“[Mass Cleanse].”
The filth on the ground, the Rubirel Guard’s armor, and even the dirt on Osthia’s scales from the fighting—some blood from her wounds that had broken open—all vanished.
She tingled. And she swore the Purifier grew slightly bigger. It turned.
“{Filth detected. Cleansing.}”
It fired the spell around it, cleaning everything—even sucking some of the dirt up and leaving bare, polished stone around it. Then it seemed to detect the Drakes, Gnolls, and Humans surrounding it. The Purifier stared down.
“{Non-citizens in noncompliance. Genetic viability 33%.}”
It gazed down at Merls. He raised his claws.
“I am from Salazsar. In the name of the City of G—”
The Purifier drew a sword.
“{Eradicating}.”
It slashed through Merls, hit one of the Rubirel Guard who had tried to block the blow, which tossed Maisy across the ground. The cut was bloodless. Merls’ torso and body collapsed, smoking, and the Purifier studied the corpse.
“[Mass Cleanse]. {Eradicating}.”
It hit one of the Rubirel Guard next, and the blade didn’t shear through the armor—so the Purifier grabbed the Rubirel Guard up and squeezed. The armor shook as the Drake writhed, and Osthia slashed at the Purifier’s legs with the Sisters of Chell.
Unlike the light-soldiers, her weapons bounced off its ‘flesh’. And then she heard the armor above her screaming a warning before the enchantments gave—
The crunch was followed by that voice.
“[Mass Cleanse].”
A bloodless corpse dropped. The Purifier turned, and a bolt of lightning struck it in the head. For a second, it wavered. Then continued. Osthia slashed into its neck, and the Purifier caught her. Inspected her. She wriggled, waiting for it to crush—
It put her on the ground. Then a hand grabbed Osthia.
“Non-citizen. You are under arrest pending—”
The copies of Vnariss. They were coming up. Dozens of light-soldiers, and more by the second. They were speaking.
“A Purifier has been summoned. Witness the City of Purity’s greatest protectors.”
“Resist and you will be cleansed.”
“Analyzing non-citizens for genetic viability…”
Osthia tore her arm free and elbowed the construct holding her in the face. It did virtually nothing, but she managed to leg-sweep it and flew upwards.
“Fall back! Fall back—Sisters of Chell! On me! Hold them back!”
She flew straight at the Purifier again and saw her squad attacking the light-soldiers. They were outmatched; the Purifier was glancing around for the lightning bolt’s sender. It caught sight of a [Mage]. Opened its mouth.
The ray of light burned through the [Mage]’s barrier spells and scorched a six-foot wide hole in the ground. Osthia slashed across the Purifier’s face and her blade didn’t leave a mark. She saw it turning, reaching up for her, gently even, like someone trying to catch a butterfly it didn’t want to hurt.
Could she distract it? Shellc was shouting at her to retreat. Osthia was peering down at her squad. Not them. She couldn’t let them—
She had hopes of doing something. Right up until the ground exploded in the dig site. The second Purifier stood, wings unfurling.
It was nearly twice as big as the last one. When it flew upwards, it was slowly. But with a terrible momentum to it. Osthia gazed downwards and then saw a claw breaking the ground. And she realized there was another Purifier down there too.
One so big it was having to squeeze through the tunnels. The two Purifiers landed on the top of the dig site, and both had swords. They were chopping anyone not ‘genetically viable’ into pieces.
That—that was the only reason everyone wasn’t dead. The light-soldiers and Purifiers would slow before each [Soldier] and [Miner] they came across. The Purifiers seemed to be able to scan in less than half a second—the light-soldiers required a few seconds, and if their targets were moving, they had to re-scan.
One of the Purifiers was pursuing a band of Silverfang Gnolls. One of the mining teams—it had its sword raised, and it towered over the tiny Gnolls. It ignored Osthia trying to stab through its brain—her sword was doing nothing! She needed Georgie’s pick! Where was he? She couldn’t leave a mark with anything, and she saw the [Mages]’ magic was just as useless on the Purifiers.
The Purifier bent and picked up one of the Gnolls who’d stopped to buy the others time. He lashed out at its hand, shouting Skills. It was the huge Ekhtouch Gnoll, the [Miner].
Thamert. He froze as the Purifier spoke.
“{Analysis. Genetic viability 89.25%. Congratulations, Gnoll. You are viable for Class 1 citizenship.}”
It put him down. Thamert staggered and seemed bewildered and mildly outraged. An Ekhtouch Gnoll wasn’t even…?
No one else was passing the tests if Osthia was barely 80%. How many Drakes were even Oldblood, let alone both kinds like Osthia? Now she saw it.
City of Purity. The Purifiers were still casting [Mass Cleanse]. In fact, the Purifier that had grabbed Thamert began to attack the Gnolls, then looked down.
“{Excrement. Cow. Removing…} [Mass Cleanse].”
It pointed at a patch of ground and removed the manure. Paused. Pointed.
“[Mass Cleanse]. [Mass Cleanse]. {Marking for further cleaning.}”
It had to do it twice more before it was satisfied. Then it took two lumbering steps after the Gnolls. Stopped.
“{Excrement. Cow. Insect nest. Ant. Removing…}”
Osthia caught her breath at last as she saw the second Purifier slow. The Purifiers might be higher-grade magic, but they were as stupid as, well, Golems. They were obsessively cleaning around the dig site, and she remembered the mining tunnels. Even the mines had been paved. Was the City of Purity supposed to all be like that?
But this was no stone city, this was a literal cow pasture. She grinned as she saw the two Purifiers stall out. Right up until she realized that the light-soldiers weren’t slowing. They were marching in ranks, coming forwards—and then some idiot decided to hit them with a lightning bolt. The bolt blew apart a group of light-soldiers—and a Purifier’s head snapped up. It abandoned cleaning and raised its sword.
A half-Giant made of light, who spat a ray of light. Osthia looked around and saw her squad fleeing its footsteps. It went to stomp, and the Sisters of Chell dove aside. Osthia cried out.
“Run! Run, you idiots!”
She’d meant for them to buy a second and disengage! But they’d kept fighting. Now, the Purifier’s head swung down with slow wrath. Osthia tried to put herself in the path of it as the third Purifier’s head rose over the excavation pit. Not again.
Had they bought anyone time?
 
——
 
Desperate Sisters of Chell being lifted in the Purifier’s grasp. One of the Sisters was pinned by a Drake light-construct because she could be a Class 2 citizen.
Boyd saw the Purifier taking Marrygold higher. The Sister screaming. Shouting at Boyd to run as Osthia hacked at the arm. The [Brave Knife] raised a backup blade.
She croaked as she saw the hand begin to tighten.
“[Heroic Stab].”
She plunged the tip of her dagger into the Purifier’s clawed foot. That was how big it was. Her knife actually pierced the glowing light-flesh, the first time anyone had wounded the damn thing. With the equivalent of a splinter’s amount of damage.
Boyd saw the Purifier pause, glance down at her, and she was backing up, already running. Tears in her eyes. But she kept watching Marrygold. To commit that face to Osthia’s memorial, if Boyd lived. If anyone lived.
The Purifier opened its mouth, aimed at Boyd, and exploded.
Its body detonated outwards in a flash of light, and then something hit Boyd. Tossed her through the air, screaming and pinwheeling, until Osthia caught her.
“I got you. I got—”
They landed, tumbling, and Osthia re-broke her wings and lay there, cursing. Then pushed herself up.
“Run! R—”
She turned, and Boyd glanced around. They saw Marrygold, Sadmile, the other members of her squad…sitting or lying in the grass. Staring around.
“You killed it? With a stab?”
She did? Boyd couldn’t believe it. It had popped! Like an overinflated pig bladder or water flask! She was pretty sure it wasn’t supp—
Then the smell hit her. Boyd stared down at something on her body and vomited. Osthia drew a breath and puked.
“What is—”
It was all over them. Something black and so foul that it ruined Boyd’s sense of smell in a moment. She heaved again, and that was a pleasant experience to the taste of it on her tongue. She hadn’t even gotten it in her mouth. The rest of the Sisters were even worse! It was, wait—
“Was that inside the Purifier-thing?”
Boyd turned, disbelieving, and saw the world’s largest cowpat still slopping down. Where the Purifier’s body had been—there was just compacted filth spreading outwards. The Sisters leapt up as the light-soldiers spoke.
“Purifier down. Sending for reinforcements.”
“Unacceptable levels of filth detected. Calling for emergency Purifiers.”
“Warning. Monster germination detected.”
—In the same moment, the sludge rippled, and some of it shot up. An eyestalk with a glowing magicore eye swivelled around, then a slug seemed to grow and slither out of the muck. A monster?
A filth-monster, like the ones that had just attacked the dig site. It made it three feet before a dozen light-spears skewered it. Another piece of the filth began to animate, probably because it was so concentrated.
Potentially, so magical. There was that black magicore in—Boyd and Osthia were backing away as the light-soldiers began to hack at the stuff. They were calling all kinds of alarms. Then another Purifier landed.
This one was over forty feet tall. How it had gotten out of the dig site tunnels, Boyd had no clue. Had it squeezed up here? Excavated the entire thing? Whatever the case, the Purifier swept a blade across the muck, killing whatever was germinating.
“[Mass Cleanse]. [Mass Cleanse]. [Mass Cleanse]. [Mass Cleanse]. [Mass Cleanse]—”
It was cleaning the muck up. Osthia and Boyd watched, and both had a feeling about what was going to happen next. Because, each time the spell was cast, the Purifier got larger. First, it was forty-some feet tall. Then fifty. It was trying to absorb a lot of filth, after all. About, say…sixteen feet’s worth of filth?
It almost managed it. The Purifier was about fifty-five feet tall when it stopped casting spells. It pointed a finger at the remaining puddle of moving filth.
“[Mass Cl—]”
Then it exploded. Osthia, Boyd, and the squad of Sisters saw the magic bindings of the Purifier rupture. They stared up as a rain of blackness began showering down. Looked at each other.
Then they ran for it. Then, Boyd swore she saw her crazy captain laughing. Osthia had tears running down the filth caked onto her body.
“That? That’s the doom of Naamreles?”
It was just one of those things experienced [Mages] told younger ones. Stop relying on [Cleanse] and wash your underwear. No spell’s perfect. And some young [Mage] would wonder why anyone knew that. Or wonder—if you [Cleansed] something, where did all the dirt go?
 
——
 
Wall Lord Ilvriss didn’t know what was going on with Dig Site B. He heard only chaos, Major Shellc shouting orders—then some clarity.
“We are under attack from light-constructs, Wall Lord! It’s an entire damn army and some kind of super-summons capable of flight, Tier 5 attack spells—”
Oh no. The City of Purity was awake. Ilvriss was galloping towards the dig sites, shouting the alarm in the next moment. It was Lyonette du Marquin who was too slow to follow.
“Ilvriss, wait, I’ll get Ulva and—Ishkr, go find Xitegen now!”
Ishkr ran for the portal door. Lyonette whirled.
“Someone go after Ilvriss! Tell me what’s going on—not you, Nanette—and keep in contact!”
To her relief, the witch wasn’t running after Ilvriss, but into the inn.
“I’ll watch with the [World’s Eye Theatre]!”
“Good idea! Ilvriss, don’t—he’s gone.”
She ran a few steps out into the Cowpat Plains before Ser Dalimont caught her.
“Your Highness, my arm’s broken, and you can’t endanger yourself!”
“Marquin’s remaining breast, I can’t! Let go of me, Dalimont!”
They were arguing as the door closed behind them; Liska was sending Ishkr to Invrisil, and Lyonette’s heart was in her throat.
“Why now? No one was stupid enough to dig today, surely! Did it have to be this moment? After Tolveilouka, that bastard? Could anything else go wrong?”
Someone coughed behind her.
“Er, well, funny you should mention that. Now, look. I admit, we got a bit heated. I tried to turn you into a plague thing, you said hurtful things about my master—”
Lyonette froze. Ser Dalimont drew his sword, and Tolveilouka Ve’delina Mer raised his hands.
“I’m just here t—”
Lyonette drew a crossbow and aimed it at him. He kept his hands raised. Tolveilouka had…a hole in his forehead. Dalimont and Lyonette stared through the hole and his pulsing brains, then lowered their weapons. Tolveilouka noticed and patted at the hole.
“Damn, is that still there? It stings like—listen. Things might not be going according to plan. See, I was helping you out.”
What? Neither [Princess] nor Thronebearer said a word. They just exchanged glances and stared back at Tolveilouka. The half-Elf put his hands in his pockets. Kicked a rock.
“Okay, look. I’m sorry about the dead Wall Lord. He seemed nice. Brave. Tell you what, I could reanimate his corpse? There’s some kinds of undead that grow on you. I’ll make sure he’s a nice one—well, nice as they get. I felt bad about it, really. He and I had a heart-to-heart, and I think I was respecting him near the end. Real composure in the face of death, that fellow.”
He’s not dead. Lyonette almost said that, and Ser Dalimont stepped gently on one foot. Neither one said a word. Tolveilouka glanced at them. Put his fingers together and took a breath.
“Okay, and the City of Purity…listen. I was hoping it was inactive. Turns out, it’s not. So, um, you’re about five hundred miles away from here. Great. Just close the door and I bet you they’ll get stopped before then. I’ll help! You just have to snipe the Purifiers when they’re distracted. Three-dozen in one place and even a Dragon has a bad day, and they’re sort of diametrically opposed to my nature. Hard to fight. A hundred and, well, everything’s dead. The rest of the light-armies aren’t that bad.”
Purifier. Light armies. Lyonette twitched, and Tolveilouka held up his hands.
“I know what you’re thinking, and I’m upset with me. But here’s what you need to know: they’re not perfect. Most are pretty damn big; they’re full of shit. Literal shit. That’s what [Cleanse] spells do. You think all that dirt and stuff goes nowhere? It’s in a mini-dimension attached to you. That’s why the first time any [Mage] opens a portal dimension connected to their magic it’s filled with crap if they’ve cast [Cleanse]. Normally, it’s not a problem, but if you keep doing it, well. Naamreles invented [Cleanse], and so they didn’t get the memo.”
He jerked a thumb over his shoulder and smiled.
“Actually, that’s how they killed themselves. That and selecting only the most ‘pure’ candidates for their citizenship. See, the Purifiers sweep up all the mess, but they reached a critical mass long ago. So new ones keep getting made, but once they sweep up too much shit, they explode. Then the cycle repeats. The security systems must have been fighting their own filth for, I don’t know, at least a few thousand years? Hilarious.”
He slapped his chest, shook his head.
“That’s why we buried the City of Purity; they killed themselves trying to purify their own ranks. Then their automated legions attacked everything mindlessly. No one wanted them around by that point, anyways. The problem was, it turned out their magic was good enough to keep going and doing the same damn thing. Hence why we had to bury them. There’s filth-monsters as big as half-Giants down there. Imagine being a citizen of the ‘City of Purity’, choking to death on the filth your city kept trying to clean! Those [Miners] your lot found were probably trying to escape and ran out of food and water!”
He laughed. Hesitated as he saw his audience hadn’t joined him. Tolveilouka cleared his throat.
“Ahem. So…now they’re loose, and they’ll probably execute anyone ‘impure’, which is mostly everyone. If you’re lucky, the Purifiers will explode and slow the others down, but uh, the light-armies are probably going to enslave anyone not pure, and the ‘citizens’ will be taken below where they’ll probably die of starvation. They’re—well, the Purifiers are the real threats…but the City of Purity’s armies are pretty damn…look, just close the door. I’ll throw rocks at them or something. I just need to, uh, get some weapons and heal up.”
He touched the hole in his forehead again. Winced. Tolveilouka gave Lyonette a thumbs up.
“I was helping.”
He backed up a few steps.
“I tried to. Look, you try it.”
The half-Elf turned, jogged off, hesitated, and then jogged back.
“When you think abou—”
Lyonette shot him in the face with her crossbow. Tolveilouka slowly pulled the bolt out of his nose and eyed her.
“I suppose you deserve to do that. Do it again and I’m breaking your fingers. Right…good luck with that.”
He ran off, then shouted.
“I mean it about ‘run’! You all suck if you can’t even get me to Phase 2! Stop shooting crossbow bolts at me, I’m just trying to help—”
He ran off. Lyonette and Ser Dalimont stood there in silence until the door burst open.
“Lyonette! It’s horrible! There’s Drakes made of light attacking, a-and Nanette sees more coming from below, but she can’t see the City of Purity because it’s warded!”
Hethon was waving his arms and panicking. Lyonette and Dalimont turned. After a moment, she nodded.
“We’ll be there right away, Hethon. Tell Nanette to inform everyone we know. And keep an eye on Ilvriss.”
He nodded and ran. She looked back at Ser Dalimont. He glanced around.
“Given where we were, I don’t think anyone could have seen…”
“Good. Dalimont? Not a word to—”
“Of course.”
More silence. Lyonette mouthed a few words, then exhaled.
“Helping.”
“Evidently, Lyonette.”
She felt at her face. At her arms, which had nearly turned into putrid flesh. Glanced at the ground he’d destroyed. Thought about Ilvriss.
“Dalimont?”
“Yes, Your Highness?”
“Find me a way to get on his bad side.”
“How, Your Highness?”
“I don’t know, a mean poem or something.”
Then she was running. But Lyonette didn’t forget this was definitely all Tolveilouka’s fault.
 
——
 
Wall Lord Ilvriss heard the frantic fighting as he raced towards the Cowpat Plains and the dig site at top speed. By the time Lyonette appeared, panting what she’d been told at him, he didn’t question it. He just gave orders.
“Welsca, are you there?”
“Here, Wall Lord!”
He looked around and saw her actually flying past him. She had wings. And her scales were fire-red, not his prismatic—she was trailing smoke as she panted. Ilvriss’ own wings stirred, then he just began shouting.
“Here are my orders: Evacuate Thirthoof. Evacuate the base camp, and warn every [Rancher] in the region! Tell them what’s coming, and if they don’t listen, get them to just look this way!”
He wagered they could see the light attacks and maybe even the damn Purifiers, they were so big. Ilvriss kept shouting.
“Get me Master Oidhol as well!”
“Yes, s—Master Oidhol?”
Of all the Drakes—Ilvriss ignored Welsca and fished out a speaking stone.
“Major Shellc, are you there? I want you to retreat back to our base camp or further if needed! Do not engage those constructs!”
“I hear you, Wall Lord. But it’s a damn fighting retreat. Your Captain Asrira and her squad refuse to fall back. They’ve taken down a Purifier, but they insist on holding the line.”
Osthia? Ilvriss’ head was spinning from his near-death experience. He hadn’t slept. He really wanted a lie-down in Erin’s inn. He was sharp and fuzzy, like he was dying. But he just rode, and his lungs felt like they were glittering from the inside, if that was even a sensation. He toggled the speaking stone and hit mass-communications by accident.
It didn’t matter.
“Ilvriss to all forces, fall back! That means you, [Major]!”
Welsca turned, mid-conversation with a confused Master Oidhol. Did he mean Captain Asrira? Her rank had fluctuated a bit, but—then she heard the voice coming back.
“Wall Lord? We have to hold the line. Someone has to.”
Osthia Blackwing sounded…too calm. Welsca recognized it as a warning sign from her Manus training. Shock. The [Wing Captain] was a veteran who’d lost her entire command at least once.
“The army will be wiped out, sir. Requesting permission to hold the line.”
“Denied. Get out of there, [Major]. You and your forces.”
“Nossir. Someone’s got to cover the retreat, General.”
This time, Welsca’s head snapped around, and she nearly lost control and slammed into the ground. But Ilvriss was just galloping ahead. And…
 
——
 
Lyonette du Marquin was listening from the [World’s Eye Theatre]. She could see Captain Osthia. Both wings broken, and she was reeling.
The light-soldiers had refrained from attacking them until she’d hacked the twentieth one apart. Then they’d decided she wasn’t worth protecting. The only thing that had saved her was the cloth-armor that Ilvriss had bought for her from Honored Deskie. Eight light-spears had nailed her in the chest, and she was—mostly—unhurt.
But it looked like one had hit her in the helmet. Her squad was hunkered down in Dig Site B’s camp, fighting from the fortifications there. Drakes and Gnolls were evacuating the camps, but some teams, like Maiss’, weren’t immediately fleeing.
More were doing the things Drakes did. Captain Osthia spoke muzzily as scrying spells began coming in from Salazsar.
Dramm and the other spies were calling ten kinds of alarms, and regular citizens and Wall Lords were tuning in. Not the news, not yet. No one had bothered telling them.
What they saw were light-Drakes pouring out of a hole in the ground. Vast titans with halos and wings, patterned off another species, an ideal, battling foul monsters made of sludge. And what the citizens of Salazsar heard was Wall Lord Ilvriss’ voice, cracking, panting, and Asrira Shieldscale. Shouting at each other, confused.
“Drakes don’t run, General! We can hold them.”
Osthia swung her sword through a light-Drake’s neck. She stumbled, and someone caught her. Her squad. The Goblin Lord’s army was everywhere—no, the light-constructs. She was shouting. At General Thrissiam. Or was it General Garusa? It didn’t matter. He was bellowing nonsense in her earhole.
“That’s Dragondung, [Major]! I just gave you an order!”
“Order ignored, sir. What’s best for everyone is I stay.”
Another wave was coming. Her squad—Osthia was motioning them back, but they were good soldiers. They wouldn’t run.
One could save a hundred lives. Her commander was bellowing orders as well, but General Thrissiam just shouted back.
“That’s enough. I told you to retreat, Periss! Get out of there! Please.”
Periss? Who? Osthia began to croak, then saw another Drake climbing the trenches. She kicked a face in with her boots as someone knifed the bastard.
“Sir, I’m needed here—protocol dictates the commanding officer—”
“Hang the protocol. Retreat, Periss. I can’t lose you. What good are our heroes if we have to keep making them? Please. Run.”
The [Sister of the Unforgotten] realized that Ilvriss wasn’t talking to her at last. He was talking at her. Osthia’s head turned. She snapped out of the haze and saw the wounded Sisters around her. For a moment, she saw the pile of the dead. Then General Thrissiam waving at her—
She swore she saw Periss for a second, slowly regarding her as she sat, sharpening a blade and waiting for the next battle. None of them spoke, but their eyes—
Periss, Osthia, whatever her name was, turned.
“…Fall back in order. No one dies here. Squad, give me [Lesser Acidbreath] and run.”
The glowing forms climbing the trenches were greeted by a salute of acid. They paused only a second—then they cleared the trenches. No one met them with blades at the top. They marched into the camp, and the lines were breaking. Osthia was running.
Salazsar watched Drakes running and heard Ilvriss shouting a dead woman’s name.
But if that rattled them—
They’d seen nothing yet.

Advance Miner Georgie knew what Maiss and his team were doing. Either they were panicking and grabbing their possessions, thinking they needed their pay or gear and putting that above their lives, or they were looting everyone else’s stuff in the chaos.
Fair enough, he’d done both. But this wasn’t a disaster anyone would survive. And they were his team, damnit—
“Maiss! Maiss, run, damnit! This isn’t the time t—”
He took a moment to find where the entire team had run into their tents. The makeshift barracks were more organized than most [Miners]’ messy cots with possessions strewn around. There was a temporary gymnasium next door, and Maiss’ team had always been weird.
Too many breaks. Too bad at their jobs, yet no one said a word up top. And Maiss himself…
He seemed calm as he knelt over a trunk in the center of the room. The rest of the team, Drakes and Gnolls, were shucking their clothing. Putting other clothing on, belting up—Georgie skidded to a stop, then bellowed.
“Are you insane? We have to run!”
Maiss whirled, then smiled.
“Advance Miner, you made it. Good. Get out of here. We’re doing our jobs. You’ve done yours.”
“What? Are you mad? Don’t be a hero—those light-things are everywhere, and the big ones are crushing the Rubirel Guard!”
Maiss kept pulling things out of the trunk, tossing them at his team. He adjusted his belt, and someone brought something over and threw it over his chest and began buckling it secure. A…breastplate?
Mining Team Leader Maiss glanced up, and his eyes were too calm. Not confident; there was a tightness there as he grunted.
“I know. Tier 3 spells have no effect on the big ones. Piercing Skills and high magic. Pop ‘em and the others get distracted. Advance Miner, fall back.”
“That’s armor. What’s going on?”
Georgie’s mind felt slow. Trouble he was good at detecting and running from. But what was…?
It was when Maiss stood and clipped a speaking stone into a holster at his ear that it clicked for Georgie. Maiss was wearing a metal breastplate and chainmail underneath it. He had on leg armor, even tail armor, and when he put on his helmet, only his jaw was visible; the jawguard wouldn’t fit anymore.
He grimaced and tossed the piece of metal aside. Maiss checked his belt, and he had a sword on one side with a spiked shield on the other, a backup wand, backup shortsword—then he was so familiar Georgie just blinked.
The [Soldier] turned and barked.
“Company, fall in! We’re up to our earholes in magical constructs! You heard the Wall Lord! Fall back and link with Major Shellc’s forces! Holiday’s over, boys and girls!”
“You—you were just—”
Squads of grim Drakes and Gnolls were moving out the doors, armed to the teeth in metal. Not just metal; Maiss had been tossing enchanted munitions and artifacts at his company. They wouldn’t have fit in a bag of holding with that much magic.
Maiss patted Georgie on the shoulder, then towed him towards the door.
“I told you I saw the Winter Solstice. And the Goblin Lord, and the Tidebreaker too. Do you think the Wall Lord really marched all this way north with only a token force? Sorry about the bad mining. Stick with us. Let’s go!”
Then they were barrelling out of the tents, and more teams were shedding their disguises and revealing their true colors. A rank of crossbows sank to one knee and fired; they cut down the glowing Naamreles soldiers, and then everyone was up and running. Fighting a retreat as Captain Osthia whirled.
Major Shellc’s voice was steady as it pulsed out of Maiss’ earpiece.
“Colonel, tell me your forces are ready for a fight. We’re headed to Fallback Point B. I’m going to slow the advance of the constructs with our Gem Regiments, but they won’t last long. Do not engage those Purifiers. Wall Lord Ilvriss has a plan to delay them, which means we’ll only be facing the constructs.”
“Yessir, Major, we are on the move. Only a few legions of Naamreles’ finest?”
“That’s the spirit, Colonel.”
Then Georgie saw a real army running and moving into place. His mouth was still open as he ran. He turned—and Captain Osthia was just as dumbfounded as her squad whooped and cheered.
In her case, she’d forgotten Ilvriss’ plan.

Ulva Terland’s eyes narrowed as she saw Drake [Soldiers] pouring out of the dig site. They were making for a seemingly-unmarked stretch of grass miles away from their base camp. [Miners] were milling about, but an entire third of the original dig force had revealed armor and weapons.
“That damn Drake brought a real army north. I knew it!”
“Under the circumstances, Aunt, we should be so lucky. What are we going to do?”
Xitegen was panting as he jogged in the scrying orb. She glanced at him; she was in Invrisil, counting the damage that half-Elf had done, and she’d been organizing a taskforce to wipe him out for good and his damn home.
Now this. Her temples hurt. Ulva snapped at Xitegen.
“Do? That fool’s the one who unearthed all this!”

“Silence. Where are you, Xitegen?”

Primera, Seconda, and every Golem he had was running with him, she realized. Ulva Terland hissed.

Still repairing himself? Ulva Terland closed her eyes and sensed—

Timekeeper was striding into the streets of Invrisil when Ulva Terland kicked open a window and leapt out.
He caught her, of course. She snapped as the Terlands rushed out; half their Golems were marching with him!
“Timekeeper! What are you doing? You’re abandoning your post!”
“The City of Purity has awakened, Lady Terland. I am going to stem their forces. With-out combatting them, they will reproduce infinitely.”
Her mouth opened—then compressed into a line.
“Define infinitely.”
“Any magical po-wer source will generate more Purifiers or their light-soldiers, Lady Ul-va. Without restriction, they will advance and conquer. The people of Naamreles are dead. Hence their burial by all forces. The folly of Naamreles must not spread.”
“This isn’t the first Walled City I’ve heard of being buried. Who puts all their problems in the damn dirt? Can’t the Drake handle it?”
The Matriarch of House Terland was complaining, but Timekeeper saw her checking her side as he strode towards the portal door.
“Burial is an acceptable practice when one is out of armaged-don class spells, Lady Ulva. I am informed by your predecessors they run out very quick-ly. Naamreles has barriers. I request reinforcements.”
She said nothing. But she let him put her down and strode into The Wandering Inn. It was chaos there. Timekeeper could ‘hear’ the [Message] spells and unsecured communication spells around him.
Drakes requesting aid from Pallass, who was slow to react. The City of Gems watching their Wall Lord, too far removed to act immediately.
Hesitation.
He had none. A Golem was waiting for him with a panting [Diplomat]. Yweine lifted a repaired hand.
“My directive is to keep Wall Lord Ilvriss alive.”
He nodded once at her. But halted; Lady Ulva Terland had not made up her mind. She was scowling.

“By your will, Lady Terland.”
Timekeeper advanced through the door as Xitegen began arguing, but Ulva Terland was notoriously stubborn. All Terlands were.
He just hoped she made the right choice.

The infinite legions of Naamreles would have made even Nerrhavia’s Fallen’s Golden Hordes hesitate. For they were no Hemp-caste, who still breathed and bled and died.
These were a true force without care for their lives, and led by the Purifiers, they were advancing on the retreating forces of Salazsar. To judge whether they were worthy of Naamreles’ mercy.
The Purifiers were the most powerful constructs by far. They could fire Tier 5 [Dawnbreak Ray] spells from their mouths at will or activate Tier 6 [Sunburst Field] spells to clear enemy soldiers. At need be, they could link and project Tier 7 magic.
They had been made to slay horrors like Tolveilouka the Wretched. With their flight, catching the escaping Salazsarian forces would have been easy.
Unless they were delayed. 
The thing stopping the Purifiers was the Cowpat Plains themselves. Even as more and more appeared—and the City of Purity had too many, hundreds—each one became distracted with the…the filth.
In Naamreles’ orbit? Unacceptable! The Purifiers were no beings capable of thought. They did not see that the cleared ground around the City of Purity no longer remained. The pristine tiles that had eradicated all life for miles upon miles around the Walled City were long gone. Buried. But they behaved as if it were still there, purifying the manure. Purifying the dirt.
—Still, more kept flying upwards. There was no way to kill them unless they were too full and ‘popped’; not all of them were at a critical mass. Someone had to do something.
Like Master Plumber Oidhol. He was no hero. He was just a working [Plumber], if one of the best in Salazsar. He was self-conscious of always smelling slightly like the pipes he worked on. No one really respected a [Plumber] until you needed them. He had a stable job, though, family, sons who were taking up the family business, even if they were worried no one wanted to marry their daughters to a [Plumber].
Just a Drake who’d gotten an offer to work for that famous Wall Lord. And he’d thought…why not? Told his family he’d never be near any danger because he was just a [Plumber]. Who needed a slightly overweight Drake losing his neck-spines? He’d laughed about it.
“Master Plumber, they’re coming!”
Oidhol was up to his knees in sewage. He was wrapping pipes to form the worst joins in his entire life with sticky tape, fusing metal together with every trick he had. He and his helpers—
“I’m almost done!”
“Hurry!”
He should have been running. He could have, and no one would have blamed him, but Ilvriss had said—
Oidhol heard that voice from behind him.
“Non-citizens, this is your final warning. Analysis: 57.5%. Non-citizen, you are not qualified for—”
Fighting. The [Soldiers] in Thirthoof were trying to evacuate the panicked Humans. Most had ridden off, but this last batch was covering Oidhol—the Drake’s claws slipped. Instantly, he was sprayed with something so foul he didn’t think about it.
“[Emergency Stoppage]. Almost—bend them upwards.”
“Master, they’ll rupture—”
“They just have to last for a few minutes! I don’t care what the pressure is! Hurry!”
Frantically, the [Master Plumber] worked, and he heard screams, shouting. The voices.
“Analysis: 45.63%. Non-citizen—”
Closer.
“Analysis—”
Sweat running down his back and scales. He was thinking of his children, but there were children here, and people’s lives were on the line. 
A voice.
“Analysis: 30.88%. Non-citizen. You are under arrest. This is a military operation. Resist and you will be executed.”
Master Oidhol raised his claws slowly and saw the pipe was done. Jutting upwards, and there was a tower stack built by the other [Plumbers]. The ugliest mess he’d seen, already leaking, but his [Emergency Stoppage] Skill was the only thing holding this all back. He peered up, and a Drake with a smile and a glowing face, his Ancestor, was pointing a spear down at him.
“Non-citizen. Move towards the wall.”
The [Plumber] didn’t respond. He just gripped the pipe and hoped like hell it made a difference. The Wall Lord needed miracles and heroes. Dragons witness him—Oidhol was neither.
But he was a damn good [Plumber]. He lifted the [Emergency Stoppage], and the pipes rumbled like the digestive system of the greatest beast in the world. The glowing Drake hesitated.
“Non-citizen—”
Then Oidhol felt the pipes shudder and grinned. A Wall Lord’s idea. Madness. Practically a war crime in the world of plumbing. Oidhol couldn’t believe he was doing this again. It had been nigh on forty years since he’d built a system that emptied the septic system.
When he was a boy, he’d flooded an entire tower of Salazsar. Now? The [Master Plumber] had aimed the pipes where the desperate Wall Lord had told him they were needed.
Straight up.

Marvus Lischelle couldn’t believe his eyes. It was like the end of the damned world. His world. The glowing Drakes kept coming, and those horrific, huge ones had killed everything. The town of Thirthoof wasn’t burning, but it was being swept by the shining figures.
He had his hat in his hands. This was all under their feet? Had the half-Elf woke them up? Or Ilvriss?
“They’re not gonna stop. Evacuate everything. We’ll never save the herds. Just…just open the pastures and let Big Burlap and the other bulls take their herds and…”
His voice was hoarse. He saw the Purifiers flying over the city. Blasting anyone they didn’t like. Even the cows.
Even the horses! They left only one alive; the rest weren’t, what, good enough? One was taking aim at the [Mayor], Bootsy, who was riding out with the last group. Marvus reached for his side, but he was too far away. The Purifier’s mouth glowed—
And then something exploded skywards, and it swerved. Stopped. Marvus squinted down.
“The hell’s that?”
He saw a weird, circular white cap on the ground he didn’t recognize. Wait, wasn’t that the ‘sewer system’ that Bootsy had been talking about? The one Aronia wanted? The Drakes had capped the old shit-lake next to the town. But what was…
Something was spraying upwards. Loosed by a [Master Plumber] and a Wall Lord’s Skill. [Adaptive Plumbing] plus the systems that Oidhol had installed were all being funneled into a few pipes, and the pressure was squirting what Marvus realized had to be the most disgusting liquid in the Cowpat Plains skywards.
That was saying something given all the competition. The liquid sewage nearly hit one of the Purifiers in the face, and they turned.
They might have had kill-orders in their programming, but the sight of a fountain of…the Purifiers broke off their strafing runs instantly and began to [Mass Cleanse] the fountaining feces.
Or tried. It just kept coming. Marvus began laughing despite himself. The famous City of Purity, buried in the Cowpat Plains; the irony was not lost on him. Even so—he saw the Purifiers slow down and begin bloating again. That still left thousands of glowing Drakes marching towards Salazsar.
A flash of lightning split the skies. One of their Gem Regiments had just blown a company to pieces with lightning. Marvus wished that would do it. Or all the Drakes that the Wall Lord had hidden from even him.
“That bastard could have beaten the lot of us like drums. Shame…”
Marvus whispered.
“I don’t think he brought enough [Soldiers].”

Vnariss Stulvecrell was not the only Drake marching for the glory of the City of Purity. Nor was it even only Drakes.
A female Gnoll with a tall helmet marched into position, raising bows and extolling the virtues of the City of Purity with him. After all, the Walled City had taken every species.
So long as they aligned in thought.
And of course, later, so long as they were the best. Not the most pure of bloodlines, oh no. Just the best. The most attractive, the strongest, the—
The Drakes who fought in their glowing armies were not the regular civilians, of course. They were the soldiers who had won citizenship by being the best. By volunteering their faces and identities into forever.
Vnariss was beaming as he marched.
“A determination has been made. A foreign army is assailing the City of Purity. Purifiers, Light Armies of Naamreles, defend your home. Mandate: all Class 1-applicable citizens are to be taken alive at all costs. Mandate: The Putrid One’s minions are to be destroyed at all costs.”
A thousand of him spoke with the same voice. Walked with the same surety he had in life. Alongside him, the Gnoll, Incorra Wild Wastes, swung her bows up.
“For the glory of the City of Purity. All are welcome who shall produce a finer age. All those who would sully it be cleansed.”
Vnariss agreed.
“In the name of our tired City of Purity, advance.”
They marched. The Drakes and Gnolls were forming a battle-line in the distance, and the advance Light Soldiers were pursuing. But at a march; they did not run. They ignored arrowfire, spells that cut some down; they were hardy, enduring.
Not as tough as Golems, but not as expensive. Not as adaptive as summons, but far more mass-producible. The ultimate soldier, some had called them. So many made that claim, but Naamreles’ finest—
Vanished as another bolt of lightning crashed down. Light Gnolls were sent flying. A bolt of lightning blew apart 57 of Vnariss’ number, dissolving their light-bodies.
His head turned. The Drake identified a unit of Drakes slamming spears down on the ground, and the dark thunderclouds overhead. He spoke as he marched.
“Hostile magics detected. Erchirite Spears confirmed. The City of Gems. Erchirite Spears below legion-strength; no additional strategy required. Countermeasures deploying.”
As he spoke, the light-soldiers bunched up, not moved apart. And a glowing nimbus of light appeared over their heads. They became units of a hundred, and each one had an umbrella-shield that covered their main mass.
One of the shields took another flash of lightning, and it nearly winked out—but it had protected the light-soldiers below from destruction, and it would reform in six minutes. If they were destroyed, well, the goal was not to preserve any one light-soldier but merely increase their viability in combat as long as possible.
There would be more.
They engaged in combat as some of the Vnariss light-soldiers met the rearmost elements of the retreating Drakes. Loss ratio: 55-0.
Vnariss once again turned his head and studied the unit fighting without casualties.
Again, he spoke.
“Rubirel Guard confirmed. Rubirel Guard below legion-strength; no additional strategy required. Countermeasures deploying. Salazsar’s hostility has been logged. No Flawless Gemstone Regiments detected on the field. Battle shall commence in regrettable victory.”
At his words, the formations changed again. From a hundred soldiers marching together, they became…ten. Not because the groups split up. Rather, ten soldiers walked into each other, forming balls of light which shifted and revealed new figures. Larger. Giant soldiers stepped out of the orbs of light, forming squads once more. Giant versions of Vnariss. Armed with warhammers.
It was a suboptimal use of their numbers—unless fighting heavy armor. The gigantified Drakes advanced in a killing line ahead of regular infantry. After all, Naamreles had fought Salazsar before.
Vnariss’ copies had done so many times…Incorra walked next to him, hundreds of Gnolls smiling and aiming bows up, waiting to come into range.
“Praise the City of Purity. Condemnation to the traitorous City of Gems. They’re still around. Good. Perish, traitors to Drake-kind. Set us free.”
Forwards. The two walked and saw, ahead of them, something the City of Purity didn’t respect, even if it had always needed. The specialty of Salazsar, so both smiled, though they had never really stopped.
Digging.
