Foreman Rolx was digging. He knew they were about to be attacked, but he was digging because, well…someone had to.
His pickaxe was faster than a shovel. He was out-digging three whole teams, who stared at him until he roared at them to hurry up. Because they were digging…trenches.
Trenches and a wall. It made sense. You dig a trench, you get dirt. Put the dirt into a wall.
Earthworks. When he’d told Major Shellc, the Drake had asked him if he could really dig even a small trench that fast. Because he was used to making [Soldiers] do it. Soldiers without Skills.
This was just soft earth. Rolx had already made the trench ten feet deep. Which didn’t mean a wall ten feet high, but it was getting there. [Miners] were packing rocks into the ground, and [Soldiers] were assembling.
Advance Miner Georgie nearly fell into the trench when he and Maiss’ team reached them last. The legions of light-soldiers were a ways behind them; they were slower and taking fire.
“Georgie! Get down here! Maiss too!”
When Maiss’ team didn’t move, Rolx swore and howled up at them; even they’d be useful, but Georgie tumbled down into the trench.
“Maiss is fighting up there!”
“He’s what? Clear everything around us! Just swing the pickaxe; it processes everything into dirt cubes! Someone will grab it with a bag of holding—go!”
He and Georgie began swinging their pickaxes until they ran out of mana. Or at least, Georgie’s did. Rolx’s just recharged as he used a Skill, and Georgie nearly spat out his cigar stub.
“Rolx, Maiss’ team are all undercover soldiers! They’re from Salazsar!”
“What? Really? Damn, we might just survive this. Keep digging!”
“How deep?”
“How tall are those giant Purifiers? That deep! But we’re building a slope. Give them a hill to run up!”
“Ancestors, why aren’t we running?”
The two kept digging, swearing, but both were thinking the same thought.
Can’t run forever. Someone had to make a stand, right? And both of them had magical pickaxes. Rolx was no fighter, but he’d seen how effortlessly the pickaxes took out light-soldiers. Better than the damn Rubirel Guards. If…
Then, and only then, did Wall Lord Ilvriss make it to them. Rolx heard the shouting from above and grabbed a rope; then after three pulls, gave up on climbing it and excavated a ramp because like hells he was young enough to pull himself up a rope all the way to the top.
Wall Lord Ilvriss was there. Shouting orders at Major Shellc, searching for Captain Shieldscale, talking with a ghostly Lyonette and even Lord Xitegen. Rolx listened, panting, gulping down water, and saw the light-soldiers were less than five minutes away. Already, light-arrows were raining down, but several hundred feet short of the trenches.
For now. He saw Maiss’ team armed and ready to go on the makeshift walls. And Ilvriss…he was speaking to Clan Leader Plisce. The terrified people from Riverfarm.
The civilians. When he saw Rolx, he motioned the Gnoll over, and Rolx’s stomach twisted. He and Georgie glanced at each other and walked forwards.
I have a family. I’ll…Rolx hesitated.
He wavered—and the Wall Lord spoke.
“All non-combat classes will evacuate the area now! Head towards the [Door of Portals]; if it cannot hold enough, Welsca, take them down the roads. Foreman Rolx!”
“Wall Lord—I’m ready.”
Ilvriss turned to Rolx, and the Gnoll swallowed hard as Georgie looked at him. But it had slipped out. Ilvriss slowed, then grabbed Rolx’s arm.
“Good. Get your people to safety.”
“Wall Lord? But—”
“I said non-combat classes out. Aren’t you a family man?”
Ilvriss didn’t wait for a response. He strode to the head of the line of Drakes and Gnolls. Soldiers. Ones he’d served with personally.
Maiss had been at the Winter Solstice. He and his company were gritting their teeth, aiming down at the oncoming legions, but they had to remember the Draugr. If this was not a hundred thousand Draugr—there were no other armies.
Just them. Xitegen was watching Ilvriss. So was Lyonette and Ulva Terland. So was his city and the [Ranchers], but the Wall Lord didn’t see any of them. He just walked down the line of [Soldiers], who glanced at him for something. Hope. Inspiration. He turned, peered at Osthia and Major Shellc, and gave them his best.
Ilvriss cleared his throat and triggered a [Loud Voice] spell. He spoke in that crisp, even impartial, tone he used at company events.
“Attention, all employees. Combat pay will be doubled for the duration of this engagement.”
Rolx stopped searching for a place to run. The Silverfangs stopped saddling horses and howling the alarm. Even the [Soldiers] lifted their helmets or eyed each other.
Ilvriss went on, steady.
“The same will apply to overtime bonuses. At this moment, all civilian classes will be evacuated from this area; this is a House Gemscale combat operation. With that said, I intend to hand out substantive rewards for all those participating in combat…”
Lyonette’s mouth was slightly open. She’d been possibly preparing for her own Marquin-type speech. Xitegen was cleaning one ear with a pinkie as he eyed Ilvriss.
But this was the style of the Wall Lord of Gems. And Rolx thought, after he actually stopped panicking—
Did Ilvriss change his scale color or something? Did he always have wings?
 
——
 
This was Ilvriss’ style. He was no Zel Shivertail. He could not say ‘follow my tail’ and plunge into combat. Nor was he even Lyonette or Erin.
He was Ilvriss all the way down. Cut him in half and you’d just get Ilvriss. He might have changed species, but that just made him…
Extra Ilvriss.
He was listing their combat benefits. Informing them about overtime pay. He could sense the [Soldiers]’ confusion. And you know what?
Maybe that was part of the plan. Talk like this was something predictable, and [Soldiers] who thought this was it, the final battle, stopped getting ready to shit themselves or run. Tell them that this was the life-or-death last stand and they’d fight like hell or treat it like that.
Tell them they were doubling their pay and they second-guessed the terror. But he was not a fool to think that alone would work, either.
Ilvriss adjusted the speaking stone.
“This is it, ladies, gentlemen, Selphids, if we have any. The City of Purity has been uncovered. The method was less than ideal. There will be an investigation, but this is what I came here to find. What I hoped we’d find. A Walled City’s treasure. And…its doom.”
He pointed, and they beheld the shining legions. The growing Purifiers absorbing the filth. One exploded as Ilvriss watched, and the others covered it. Like glowing butterflies glomming into a flower made of crap.
He wished his life involved less plumbing mishaps. Ilvriss recalled trying to unstick a toilet as Erin ran commentary and grinned.
A smile without fear. He didn’t know how it appeared to the others as he walked, calmly, down their lines. Meeting their eyes. Speaking as if he were at an office meeting. But with a passion that grew as he pointed.
“I don’t intend to risk anyone’s life I don’t have to. Clan Leader Plisce, workers from Liscor, Invrisil, Celum, Riverfarm, I will ensure that House Gemscale rewards you fully for your efforts regardless of whether or not I personally survive. But every [Soldier] and military consultant? We have to hold this ground. The City of Purity is going to advance, and there are people here who didn’t ask for a disaster. Well, we’ve brought it to them.”
The [Ranchers]. The people of Thirthoof, who’d been damned unpleasant. Ilvriss nodded.
“I don’t like them. I don’t know how you feel, but they’re still innocent. We’re House Gemscale. We clean up our own messes. More than that…look. Just look.”
He pointed, and the identical Drakes smiled at him. Marching as light arrows struck within fifty feet of him. But even they seemed to be listening, or it was Ilvriss’ mind playing tricks on him. The Wall Lord rasped.
“This…is our legacy. Sons and daughters of Salazsar, no, people of Izril—look. This is the folly of Drakes, the madness of Walled Cities. Our responsibility. It has always been here. Waiting until we were brave enough to confront it. I don’t know what the City of Purity was. Naamreles’ name has been all but lost to time. But I can see it now. The time has come to judge a Walled City’s sins. So: hold this line. If we need to, we will retreat, but it’s there.”
He clenched a fist, and his lungs felt like they wanted to expel something. Ilvriss coughed, and a plume of glittering dust engulfed him. He waved it away.
“A Walled City’s sins and treasure. This is my promise to you soldiers: whatever we take, you will keep. Not all of it, but if you fight with me, you will carry a helmet, a spear—that bow.”
He saw something and pointed. One of the light-soldiers in the form of a Gnoll had a real bow, not a fake one. She’d been firing actual arrows skywards. A captain-version of the soldiers? Now that he looked, more than one light-soldier had a real weapon or piece of armor.
Loot from other armies they’d destroyed? Ilvriss peered around.
“Take them down, and claim the City of Purity’s treasures. Don’t let anyone take it from you. I’m tired of sitting on a mountain of treasures that will never be used. Now’s when it matters. So…”
He had no closing statement to this speech. It felt like even the light-soldiers were waiting for Ilvriss to finish, marching a touch more slowly. The Wall Lord blinked, then shrugged.
“House Gemscale, prepare for combat.”
Ancestors, that sucked. He pumped a fist up in the air and went striding towards Xitegen to beg the [Lord] for help—and nearly jumped into the air when he heard the roar of sound behind him. Ilvriss turned, and they were cheering.
Colonel Maiss stood up with his company as the first light-soldiers broke into a run. The Drake set his jaw and exploded upwards. He impaled a grinning version of Vnariss on an enchanted blade and kicked another version of the Drake down the slope.
Next to him, a Gnoll fired point-blank into a Drake’s face, then ran through another with a spear. Major Shellc hopped over the dirt wall, and his sword slashed around him, then he leapt back up, having cleared a hole.
“You heard the Wall Lord! Hold the line! Salazsar and the Walled Cities!”
Ilvriss saw people taking cover as the light arrows began to rain down. But no one was running.
Brave people. He wondered how they did it. But then, no one had accused Ilvriss of being perfect. He could lack for introspection a lot of the time.
 
——
 
Ulva Terland didn’t arrive the moment that Salazsar engaged with Naamreles. She saw and heard everything, of course, but the scowling [Matriarch] ignored Xitegen until she could see the battle.
“Pretty.”
That was her first comment. At a distance, it was like glowing lines of light assailing that dirt wall. Naamreles, it transpired, was a big fan of attacking the enemy where they were strongest. After all, they could keep sending forces.
“Those Purifiers are advancing. Is the Drake buckling?”
“He’s not, Great Aunt, but when the Purifiers hit him—”
“Why are they different sizes?”
“They’re full of excrement.”
Ulva’s brows snapped together, and she had to get an abbreviated explanation. Then she rolled her eyes.
This is the doom of Naamreles? Well, despite Ilvriss’ tricks, a few Purifiers were joining the fighting. The rest were still ‘cleaning’ and seemed to be making zero progress given the literal plains of shit, but three were lurching forwards, and they were big. Big, as in ‘thirty feet tall’ for one of them.
“They pop like grapes?”
“If you can hurt them, Great Aunt. Lightning bolts fail. So if you’d like us to help…”
She said nothing. Ulva Terland was aware she wasn’t the only group who’d come to witness this madness. Lady Desinee El was holding a handkerchief over her nose.
“Oh no. It’s the Solstice all over again…he’s doomed. He needs help!”
Desinee had a weapon in hand. The Kaalglaive, for all she thought it was a stupid weapon. She appeared ready to charge, despite being in a riding dress. And she was saying that a bit too loud and glancing at Ulva.
“Lady Ulva, perhaps in this case…”
Lord Moltin began nervously. The Terlands who hadn’t gone into hiding, like Alorelle, were eying the armies, and Ulva just grunted.
“Great Aunt, it would be terrible if we let Drakes do all our work. On our lands?”
Xitegen’s voice had that overly patient sound. Ulva just narrowed her eyes.
“Shut up, boy. I’m waiting.”
“Great Aunt, with utmost disrespect, I will disinherit myself if this is how much backbone we have left in House Terland. Give me a damn good reason or I’ll—”
She finally saw what she was searching for and cut him off.
“Xitegen, I’d have you spanked like half the family deserves if you weren’t needed. I made my proclamation, or have you all forgotten? I wanted to see if they’d step up or not. There’s nothing commendable about following Golems into battle. They do all the hard work.”
It took him a moment to figure out what she meant. But Ulva had been watching for something other than the battle. She nodded at Timekeeper.
“Magnification.”
He obligingly had a Golem with a built-in telescope magnify the spot she was looking at, and Ulva sighed.
There they were. Did they think her words were meaningless? Well, even he’d probably forgotten, but they hadn’t.
“It’s more than a class. It’s a duty. If they’d failed their first test, I would have taken it back.”
What she was looking at was a group of [Riders]. Rather—a lot of [Riders], not all of the same party. More were coming.
Ulva nodded, so self-satisfied that everyone wanted to shove her.
Yweine did.
 
——
 
Marvus Lischelle was swearing with nerves for two reasons. One—he wasn’t doing the sensible thing and running for the hills, but this was his land. His land in actuality, as Aronia had reminded him. There was nowhere else for their herds to go.
And he’d heard what Ilvriss had said. A Walled City’s treasures. So he’d told Aronia to grab all the kids and pack their valuables, then taken every [Rancher] he could. They were armed with bows, mostly, but they did have long, light spears they used to kill monsters from horseback.
Not a damn army. But if Ilvriss’ Drakes broke, then Marvus didn’t see a good way to push this City of Purity back. Not with the Terlands doing jack-all.
“We waiting around here until we’re growing moss, Marvus?”
“Shut it, Nithle. I’m thinkin’. I’m thinking the only chance we’ve got is to hit ‘em and run off. No sense in treating this like a brawl. Or is there?”
The Drakes had swords and armor, but they were all light. Marvus had seen them getting knocked about, but the [Ranchers] didn’t have armor. He amended his statement.
“Maybe there is. Don’t ride at the ones with bows; they’ll shoot us out of the saddle. Keep riding, keep shootin’.”
“What happens when we run out of arrows and magic from our wands? Hatchets and light spears against them?”
One of the Golva boys wanted to know. Marvus spat.
“No. No. Hey, how many of your lot know how to lasso anything at speed?”
“Everyone’s got a lasso Skill or just knows how for fun.”
The tricks you could do with a loop of rope, and not just for grabbing a runaway steer. Marvus nodded.
“I reckon those Drakes’re as light as can be. What if we rode on ‘em, and each one of us…”
“—Gave them a mile-long drag? Dead gods, Marvus, that’s nasty!”
“Well, these ones ain’t got skin to rub off, but I reckon it’d do for them what it does for anything else. Hit and go. As for the herd—”
All the [Ranchers] turned their heads, and Marvus felt uneasy. There were two reasons Marvus was uneasy.
One: the City of Purity waking up and legions of Drakes made of light trying to kill anything that moved.
Two: Big Burlap was behind him and there was no fence.
The giant bull was, in fact, free. He and five other prime bulls were pawing the ground and eying the glowing Drakes with a distinct lack of fear. Behind them were about four hundred head of cattle.
Not prime cattle. In theory, prime beef, but not all of them were the best for meat or milk. Rather….they were the most ornery, most dangerous bulls—and cows—that each ranch family had.
Man-killers, some of them. Or just heavy and mean. It was a miracle they weren’t trying to kill the [Ranchers], who were almost as nervous about them as the glowing Drakes. But Marvus had had a word with Big Burlap.
He never knew how much the bull got, but he was a product of Skills and breeding. And the bull could choose when he wanted to murder.
Right now, a bunch of magical Drakes seemed to beat the [Ranchers]. The herd were pawing the ground, defecating, but ominously silent. Marvus hoped that when the [Ranchers] went, the herd did too.
Then he didn’t want to be anywhere in front or behind them. Marvus had a force that would have given the Drakes a run for their money if Ilvriss didn’t shoot them all dead. But he was hesitating.
Am I doing this? Coming to a Wall Lord’s defense? I could let him hang out to dry. I bet Ulva Terland’s thinking the same thing. This wraps up Salazsar in a neat bow, don’t it? They started this mess.
But the fellow’s been honest as I can see. Even fought the damn half-Elf. Sticks in the throat to let him die fighting.
Marvus was conflicted. He kept waiting as another Purifier began to lumber Salazsar’s way. He saw the Silverfang Gnolls moving away, their entire tribe, and the [Miners]. The Wall Lord was getting his people out. Decent of him.
Damnit. It was decent of him. Marvus felt like he was on the brink of everything he knew and had known being proven untrue. Drakes being heartless bastards who deserved nothing more than an arrow between the eyes had run up against the Wall Lord’s actions again and again, of late. Now, he was wavering. Like he and Aronia were balanced on a board of wood. And he didn’t know which way he’d land. He just needed a damn push.
 
——
 
That was what was needed. Ilvriss was fighting for his life; they’d lost track of him in the battle as the dirt fortifications were overwhelmed by another wave of Drakes. Welsca and everyone else was fighting in the confusion, and the people watching on the scrying orb weren’t able to tell who was winning.
Which meant that Salazsar was losing, if only by attrition. Because another wave would come. And another. The other groups had to act. Someone had to compel them to act.
Someone who could bridge north and south. Speak between species. Someone with the authority to make the Terlands move, stir the hearts of stubborn [Ranchers] and, possibly, bulls.
Like a daughter of the most famous nation of diplomacy ever.
A [Princess], perhaps. Or the greatest [Diplomat] of Salazsar.
Lyonette du Marquin appeared in a flash of light next to Ulva Terland. The [Matriarch] of House Terland’s head rose slowly. Her permanent glower shifted to Lyonette. The [Princess] glanced around, eyes flashing. She drew her breath and said—
“What are you waiting for, you old hag?”
Ulva Terland recoiled. Lyonette jumped—whirled—and Lady Damia Reinhart ran through the [Princess]. She had leapt out of a black carriage that had just parked itself on the ground.
The Unmarked Coach and its driver, Karsaeu-Dequoa, was swallowing hard as she stared at the City of Purity unearthed. Because that—
That was before even the Djinni’s time. She had come straight from Invrisil to here. A bunch of women were bailing out of the carriage as well.
Varnie and her gang were armed for a fight. However, all the gear they’d purchased was for hypothetical Golems. The [Gang Leader] took one look at the army of Drakes and started swearing.
“Oh no. C’mon. I was ready to maybe fight a few damn Golems. But this? This is way beyond any damn debt! Look! Even she’s chickening out!”
She pointed at Ulva Terland, whose head snapped around, but Lady Damia just shouted at the Terlands.
“Are you mad? Can’t you see what Ilvriss is doing? First he fights the half-Elf for you—and the 6th [Princess] of Calanfer—and now he’s waging a literal war and you’re doing nothing? Is the honor of the Five Families, of House Terland, worth nothing?”
“Rich coming from a Reinhart—”
Ulva began, and Lyonette blinked as Moltin, Nouzcrat, and the other Terlands hesitated. One of the younger [Ladies] perked her head up. Damia swung around, eyes flashing.
“That Drake just fought a horror from the Age of Myths for you! He nearly died—you thought he was dead too! Princess Lyonette almost turned into something horrific—and this isn’t the first time they’ve fought this horror! Do you need more proof they’re on the right side?”
“Er, yes. Totally unprompted. Evil half-Elf.”
Lyonette was having trouble mustering the, ah, unbridled righteous passion that Damia had. Another fault of Tolveilouka. But Lady Damia had spotted the Silverfangs. She waved her hands at Clan Leader Plisce, and shouted at the [Miners] led by Foreman Rolx.
“What are you all doing? Ilvriss is fighting for his life, and it’s the City of Purity.”
“…But it’s an army.”
Plisce pointed at the glowing Drakes and the giant Titan-Drake with a halo, wondering if Damia couldn’t see them. The [Lady] spread her hands as she cast around.
“I know. I’m not blind. But this is it. A Solstice event. This is like the Meeting of Tribes, don’t you see? This—this is going to change Izril. For the better or worse. And you want to just run? I’m not saying charge them, but you’re Silverfangs! You have bows! And [Miners] have weapons—”
Her audience were staring at her. Damia pointed.
“Didn’t you hear Ilvriss speaking? The treasures of a Walled City are right there. Right there. Haven’t you wanted to be someone important? If you run now, you can say you helped dig up the City of Purity. But if you stay, you’ll be part of that legend. Level. Level or die. I’ve levelled more in this month than I have my entire life. They say this age is changing, and I feel it. I’ll be left behind if I don’t do something. Well, this is my chance, and I see it. So what if it’s an ancient Walled City? We have the Terlands, the [Rancher] clans—a Gnoll tribe—Salazsar, and The Wandering Inn!”
Her arms spread out to encircle them all, her eyes shining.
“If we all work together, if we use the bonds we’ve forged, and the power of our disparate peoples, we’ll win. With the power of—of friendship and hope—”
She lost Ulva Terland there. The [Matriarch] recoiled physically away from that last sentence. Her face wrinkled up, and even some of the Silverfangs bit their lips. But Damia just looked around—then strode over to Lady Desinee El.
“Excuse me, Lady Desinee. You’re selling House of El products, right? Put this on my account.”
“Yes, but—hey!”
Damia grabbed the Kaalglaive.
“I need a horse—Varnie, that’s my goal.”
She pointed, and the [Gang Leader] followed the path of Damia’s finger and stared at the largest Purifier. She gaped at Damia again.
“Uh—no. Are you insane?”
Damia’s eyes flashed with the power of hard thinking.
“The Kaalblades were made to destabilize magical beings. Isn’t that right, Lady Desinee?”
“Wh—yes, but—”
Damia swung around.
“All debts paid after this, Varnie. Who’s with me?”
No one answered. So Damia grabbed Lady Desinee’s horse. She stole that too and began riding forwards. Shouting.
“For Salazsar! For The Wandering Inn and…House Reinhart! For Izril!”
She began to gallop. Plisce sat on his horse, mouth open, watching Damia race past him, until he heard a curse. Then Chief Huntress Rayna was galloping after her.
“Every Silverfang with a bow—give those Drakes some covering fire! Stay away from everything!”
She rode past a Gnoll running with a pickaxe on his shoulder. Foreman Rolx and half of Salazsar’s [Miners] had begun heading back for Ilvriss before Damia had even finished. Georgie was swearing as he hopped from foot to foot, hesitating. But then the racing Damia had company.
Her galloping horse turned its head and eyed the Human running next to the mare. The affronted horse tried to gallop faster, but Lord Xitegen Terland kept up. His Golems…
Xitegen wore the most dissatisfied expression that Ulva had ever seen on his face. She knew how he felt.
“That brat made this a hundred times more unpleasurable. I’m actually tempted to just hang it all. Friendship and hope. With a Drake.”
She spat on the ground, and Nouzcrat started.
“Ulva…”
The [Matriarch] of House Terland leapt off her dais and strode past him.
“Oh, shut up. I’m not disinheriting the only idiot who can act as Terland’s heir. Or half those children.”
Several of the younger Terlands were racing after Damia on horseback or with their Golems. Ulva Terland drew the metal wand from her side. She tapped it on Timekeeper’s side.
“I am Ulva Terland. I suffer no Drakes on my lands. I suffer ancient Drakes even less. Golems of House Terland. Let your hearts roar. [Concerto: Roil of Stone]. March!”
She lifted her wand, and Golems began to stride forwards. Like a conductor. The [Virtue of House Terland] conducting Golems like she and her sister had once done…Ulva turned her head.
“[Arpeggio Volley]. Take that Purifier out.”
A Golem with a giant ‘mouth’ planted its feet in the ground, and a spell began to gather in its center. It fired the first spell at the Purifier as other long-ranged Golems joined it. Ulva Terland’s eyes gleamed as she spun her wand.
“Light of the North—to me! Bring the wrath of House Terland south! Avoid crushing cities.”
Then she was conducting her side of the battle as Golems advanced. From safety—only an idiot got closer to a battle. But she did smile when she saw Timekeeper halt a rank of Drakes with his Skill a moment before he crashed into them like bowling pins.
There wasn’t a Terland born who didn’t love to see their Golems using their full power.

“They’re going in? We ride!”
Marvus Lischelle saw Damia charging and kicked his [Ranchers] into action. With whoops and shouts, they began to race across the Cowpat Plains, and the herd of cattle followed them. Slowly, but with an ominous building of momentum.
They passed by a disbelieving Djinni.
Karsaeu was puffing on a pipe, eying the [Ranchers] like they were mad. They wanted to throw hands with a buried Walled City? 
Both she and Lord Gorthes Reinhart, who was trying to sneak up on the Djinni, had no idea what was going on, and like hells either one was going to get in the middle of a fight.
In fact, the Reinhart had ridden over a thousand miles, and his ass was sore as he called up Cecille Reinhart and the family.
“Hey, Cecille. Cecille, pick up.”
“Gorthes? This had better be good.”
He angled the scrying orb slightly.
“Might be. Any idea why your daughter’s charging an army of glowing Drakes? The fuck’s going on here?”
He was relieved when she spat her cigarette out. Good, so he wasn’t out of the loop that much.
The rest of the family began watching.
Calidus already was.

The watchers from Salazsar couldn’t believe it. The sight of two different groups of Humans, let alone the Terlands, going to Salazsar’s defense?
“They’re flanking you! Behind you, Major Shellc! They’re going to wipe—”
Wall Lord Zail had, in fact, been screaming at Major Shellc for the last five minutes. But the [Major] had just cut him off and refused to pivot.
That idiot from Rhir—he’d refused to take a defensive position. Because he trusted Humans. But not Terlands. Not—
Zail saw one of the Golems punch through three Drakes’ heads and go storming into the fighting at Salazsar’s position. He waited for the Golem to begin attacking the astonished Salazsar soldiers, but it didn’t.
He sat back.
“But they’re Terlands.”
He was drawing breath to say something when he saw a bright, emerald figure buzzing past the Golems. An arrow hit one of the glowing soldiers, and Bird the Huntress flew over the battle.
Wall Lord Zail began choking on his spit.

“Bird!”
Nanette was screaming, but Bird had begun flying the moment she heard what was happening. She beat Elia Arcsinger by a minute, but the Named-rank adventurer just started shooting from horseback, angling her bow up.
Two [Archers]. No one but the watching people saw either at first. They just flew or found a position and began loosing arrows. Bird landed next to Elia, and they saw a hundred Gnolls with bows split off from the oncoming army.
“Ooh. A hundred versus one.”
“Two, Bird.”
“Right, whatever. Let’s see who shoots more.”
“This is life and death, Bird.”
Elia was sweating as she drew another arrow to her bow and loosed it. They were well out of the range of ordinary bows, or even Naamreles’ bows. Her arrow arced up, up—it hit one of the marching Gnolls in the nose. Bird had fired four arrows in the time it took Elia’s one.
She got one of the Gnolls in the knee and another in the shoulder. Elia paused.
“And I’m winning. That’s one. Two.”
The half-Elf fired a second arrow and knew it would hit another Gnoll before it landed.
Bird frowned, drew back on her bow, and the Chitrx-metal flexed. Bird fired, and the arrow went straight.
It refused to drop and, after two thousand feet, punched through three Gnolls, then exploded on the fourth. Elia turned her head, and the light-soldiers all stared at Bird. They began to march a bit faster.
Bird lowered her bow…then rubbed at one of her breasts.
“Ow.”
“Ah. You need a breastband for—”
“Ow, that hurt a lot.”

Everyone in The Wandering Inn was watching as Lady Damia led a charge straight into the City of Purity’s legions.
Or to be more precise—Damia charged in with Varnie and her gang. Everyone else didn’t do that.
Silverfangs took up positions on a hill that a [Shaman] raised and began setting up barricades. The [Miners] advanced onto Salazsar’s position from behind, and before they could get themselves minced, a screaming Welsca found them.
“Rolx! Don’t advance blind! I’ll find you a position—we need you to dig!”
“You what?”
The [Adjutant] was running strategy. She landed, coughing out smoke. The wings were fine, but she didn’t understand her Dragonbreath, and she was a fire Oldblood, now. She’d tried to flame the light-legions twice but only gotten smoke.
“Listen—this is a long engagement. We need your people setting up a camp and digging! The amount of earth you can shift can literally bury the enemy or form a wall! Are—are the Terlands on our side?”

“She’s not going to survive that charge. She’s insane! Listen, I need to fly—report to Major Shellc, there! He’ll assign you to a spot!”

“Marvus, are you on our side?”
“Wh—I guess so!”

The [Ranchers] had no sense of how to move in a battle. He hesitated, and then she showed him where he could ablate the enemy while they were engaged with one of the earthwork walls. She gave him credit: when he whooped and whirled his hat, everyone turned with him.
Everyone but the herd of angry cattle. They ignored the [Ranchers] and kept stomping forwards. They were headed for the center of the glowing Drakes’ mass, and Welsca cursed.

Welsca cursed again, but she flew with the [Riders]. Any idiot could see the cattle herd was going to get itself surrounded once its charge stalled out. But she couldn’t control cattle, and there was no one exactly riding a b—
Welsca’s head turned. So did Marvus’ and every [Rancher]’s. They nearly galloped into one of the trenches. But she was doing it.

Deilan El was giving orders to muster whatever [Mercenaries] and standing forces they had on offer. Kaalblades too. First the half-Elf, now this. He was pulling at his hair and trying not to tear any out when he saw someone on the cattle herd. He squinted.

This was madness. But Desinee El saw the herd of cattle about to commit to a suicide-charge, and she had to do it. She’d stolen someone else’s horse and had to do a flying leap from the panicked animal as it raced away onto the giant bull’s back.
In fairness, it wasn’t hard because Big Burlap was slowly accelerating over the ground, and there was a lot of him to land on. Nor did he ever expect someone to get on his back.
Let alone twice. His huge eyes rolled up towards her as he felt her land, and then they slowly started turning red. She felt him tense under her and hollered in one ear.
“Now listen! Aunt Maviola taught me how to speak to animals, and so did Zedalien! I know you’re smarter than regular livestock! See this? This is a Kaalblade!”
She waved one of the fake samples from her bag of holding in his face. Big Burlap snorted until Desinee spoke.
“[Product Demonstration].”
The Kaalblade snapped into life with that snap-hiss that Deilan had insisted would sell real well. She held the glowing blade up.
“It will cut anything in this world. You’re going to turn your herd or you’ll all die, got it?”
Is that a threat or an invitation? I only see them dying in my future. The bull began to trot faster, clearly ignoring her. Desinee leaned forwards and hissed in the bull’s ears.
“Listen to me. If you don’t turn, right now, I’m not going to just kill you. I’m going to hop off your back and neuter you.”
